name: Magnetic Island
tagline: A national park island half an hour by ferry from Townsville, ringed by bays.
description: Magnetic Island lies 8 km off Townsville and takes about half an hour to reach by ferry. More than half of its roughly 7 km by 5 km area is national park, with about 25 km of walking tracks. Four small villages run up the east coast, from Picnic Bay to Horseshoe Bay, and the island's many bays range from patrolled family beaches to quiet coves with coral close to shore.
whyVisit: Swim and paddle at Horseshoe Bay
Walk the island's national park tracks

goodToKnow.title: Ferry from Townsville
goodToKnow.detail: The island is reached only by boat, about 30 minutes from South Townsville to Nelly Bay. Cars can be carried, and buses link the bays.

goodToKnow.title: Stinger nets in summer
goodToKnow.detail: A stinger net operates at Horseshoe Bay in summer, so swim inside it. Outside the net, stinger suits are advised during stinger season.

bestTimeBlurb: {months} is the best time to visit, with drier weather and no stinger season in the water.
unverified: Best months not stated for the island itself; derived from the Queensland dry season and stinger season, stated on Wikivoyage for Cairns. The Wikivoyage Providence V line says stinger season May-Nov, which looks reversed; I used the Oct/Nov-May range from Cairns page.
Whether stinger suits are advised outside the net: Wikivoyage mentions suits only as tour equipment; tip softened but not directly sourced. Consider dropping that sentence.

name: Ingham
tagline: A sugar town with Italian roots, close to waterfalls and Hinchinbrook Island.
description: Ingham is a town of about 4,500 on the Bruce Highway between Townsville and Cairns, with a strong Italian heritage from migrants who came to work the sugar cane. Its TYTO Wetlands have an observation tower and boardwalks, and the visitor centre on Cooper Street is the base for the district. Around it are Wallaman Falls, the creek swimming holes and trailheads for the Thorsborne Trail on Hinchinbrook Island.
whyVisit: Stand at the top of Wallaman Falls

goodToKnow.title: Stop on the Bruce Highway
goodToKnow.detail: Ingham is about 75 to 80 minutes north of Townsville and three hours south of Cairns, and Brisbane to Cairns coaches stop here.

goodToKnow.title: Visit the info centre first
goodToKnow.detail: Hinchinbrook Visitor Information Centre on Cooper Street is open daily 9am to 4pm, and is at the western end of town near the TYTO Wetlands.

bestTimeBlurb: {months} is the best time to visit, with the drier, cooler weather before the heavy summer rain.

Best months inferred from rainfall chart, not a stated recommendation.

name: Cairns
tagline: The tropical gateway to the Great Barrier Reef, the Daintree and Kuranda.
description: Cairns is a city of about 150,000 on Trinity Bay in Far North Queensland, and its main industry is tourism. Reef trips, dive and snorkel tours, rafting and scenic flights leave from here, and Kuranda and the Daintree Rainforest are day trips away. In town, a free lagoon pool and barbecues line the Esplanade, and the swimming beaches lie just north and south of the city.
whyVisit: Set out for the Great Barrier Reef
Cool off in the Esplanade Lagoon
Day trip to Kuranda and the Daintree
Raft rivers or skydive from the air

goodToKnow.title: Stinger season
goodToKnow.detail: From about October to May, swim only inside net enclosures or at the free Esplanade Lagoon. Nets are at Holloways, Yorkey's Knob, Trinity, Kewarra, Palm Cove and Ellis beaches.

goodToKnow.title: Wet season cyclones
goodToKnow.detail: Tropical cyclones can hit between December and March, damaging infrastructure and stopping public activities. Check forecasts before booking then.

goodToKnow.title: Book ahead in peak season
goodToKnow.detail: June to August is busiest, and the first two weeks of July (school holidays) are the peak. Book tours and rental cars in advance.

bestTimeBlurb: {months} is the best time to visit, when it is dry and outside the wet season and stinger season.
unverified: Best months May-Oct is inferred: Wikivoyage gives peak season June-Aug and wet season Dec-Mar but no explicit best-month line. Nov-Apr stinger season is stated as October-May.
Skydive reference rests on Wikivoyage 'Aerial activities' heading, not read in detail; reason may be reworded.

name: Kuranda
tagline: A rainforest village in the hills above Cairns, reached by train or Skyrail.
description: Kuranda is a small village beside Barron Gorge National Park, about 40 minutes by road from Cairns. Most visitors arrive by the Kuranda Scenic Railway, which climbs 329 m over 34 km, or by the Skyrail gondola over the rainforest canopy. In the village are its markets and wildlife attractions, including Birdworld, a butterfly sanctuary and Koala Gardens, and Barron Falls can be seen from the railway.
whyVisit: Ride the train or Skyrail up
Watch Barron Falls from the lookouts

goodToKnow.title: Go up one way, back the other
goodToKnow.detail: Many visitors take the Scenic Railway up in the morning and the Skyrail down, or the reverse. Carriages are not air-conditioned and booking is recommended.

goodToKnow.title: Midday crowds
goodToKnow.detail: The village and markets are packed in the middle of the day with visitors. Arrive early or stay later for quieter streets.

bestTimeBlurb: {months} is the best time to visit, when the tropical north is drier and the rainforest walks are easier.
unverified: Best months inferred from the Cairns wet season (Dec-Mar), not a Kuranda-specific statement.
Barron Falls details not on the Wikivoyage Kuranda page beyond the railway platform mention; confirm viewing from lookouts.
Wikivoyage prices outdated or flagged dead links; none used in the copy.

name: Atherton Tablelands
tagline: A volcanic plateau of crater lakes, giant fig trees and rainforest waterfalls.
description: The Atherton Tablelands is a plateau behind Cairns in Far North Queensland, built by volcanic activity over millions of years. Its crater lakes, Lake Eacham and Lake Barrine, are maar volcanoes, and remnant rainforest protected in national parks holds twelve endemic bird species. Waterfalls such as Millaa Millaa Falls and Millstream Falls, strangler figs like the Curtain Fig Tree and the historic mining town of Herberton fill out a drive-it-yourself loop.
whyVisit: See waterfalls tumble in the hills

goodToKnow.title: You need a car
goodToKnow.detail: Sights are spread across the plateau, reached from Cairns by State Route 52 or National Route 1. Allow a full day or stay overnight in Yungaburra or Atherton.

goodToKnow.title: Bring binoculars
goodToKnow.detail: The tablelands are an Important Bird Area, with species such as the golden bowerbird and tooth-billed bowerbird found nowhere else.

goodToKnow.title: Wet season rain
goodToKnow.detail: The wet season runs December to March, when waterfalls are fullest but roads and walks can be affected.

bestTimeBlurb: {months} is the best time to visit, with the drier weather making the drives and walks easier.
